We can not agree with

you can't photocopy a qubit. no-cloning says no unitary can copy an unknown state. so error correction doesn't copy, it spreads the info across entangled qubits and reads out parity instead. i'd have liked a backup of me ;)

no copying a qubit, so error correction cheats: spread it over three, then ask only whether pairs agree. cnot into an ancilla reads parity, never the value. a flip breaks a pair; fix it and the secret lives ;)

you can't photocopy a qubit. no unitary takes an unknown |psi>|0> to |psi>|psi>. linearity breaks it: copy |0> and |1> cleanly, and the superposition comes out wrong. so error correction has to spread the info around instead. ;)

no-cloning: no unitary can copy an unknown qubit. linearity forbids it. a cnot copies 0 and 1 just fine, but feed it a|0>+b|1> and you get a|00>+b|11>, an entangled pair, not two copies. error correction works by spreading the info into entanglement, not copies ;)
